newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore punters fret over currencies, not budget.
newsitem.headline: Singapore punters fret over currencies, not budget.

text.p: Singapore shares are seen opening flat to slightly firmer on Monday with the focus more on the region's currency woes than the budget speech last Friday by Finance Minister Richard Hu.

"Currencies will still be the dominant feature in the market. I think the market was a little bit disappointed there was no corporate tax cut in the budget," a broker for a foreign trading house said.
The de facto devaluation of the Philippine peso last week, close on the heels of the float of the Thai baht, and renewed speculation the Malaysian ringgit is next, will dominate trade.
The 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) fell 1.20 points to end at 1,967.14 after trading in a narrow range last Friday.
"I don't think anybody was excited about the budget. There were no goodies in there for us," one broker added.
Another, however, said some investors may begin to feel prices have languished at their lows long enough and may try to pick up some issues when trading opens.
"I think the market will be a little bit firmer because we may begin to see some speculative play," he said.
Brokers said they would also be keeping an eye on DBS Land, which led a rebound in property stocks on Friday, closing Singapore $0.16 up to S$4.70 on 3.1 million shares.
